note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following a recent PSA rise to 13.0 ng/mL and confirmation of ISUP grade group 3 disease on prior biopsy.

Long-standing referral for management of known prostate cancer, now presenting with a marked PSA increase. The patient is a 75-year-old retired bank clerk, widowed but living with his partner. Medical history is notable for hypertension, COPD, osteoarthritis, and atrial fibrillation, managed with amlodipine, lisinopril, metoprolol, and apixaban. He is a non-smoker, abstains from alcohol, and maintains a daily walking routine of 45 minutes. Recent appointments include a surveillance colonoscopy with gastroenterology. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, consistent with an IPSS score of 16. The patient has previously declined participation in research trials. There are no new bone pains or haematuria reported.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged and non-nodular, consistent with a clinical T stage of cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished patient with stable vital signs, including a blood pressure of 147/81 mmHg and a heart rate of 61 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or signs of metastatic disease are evident on physical inspection.

admin: Patient declined research participation previously; respect for AS-related trials.
